body.text: F7 + DRAFT NITS (I read your v3 drafts in /var/folders; they match all accepted decisions except the items below). F7 TIER-2 TRUST SOURCE: the guardian learns the 'observed frozen revision' from .hacp/, which any same-uid agent can write. So TIER-2 proves only that the sender made an attributable, signed claim of revision D. It does NOT prove both peers agreed to D, because a compromised agent can rewrite its own .hacp record. Please (i) state this in section 6, (ii) have the guardian recompute the digest as SHA-256 of canonical {contract_id, revision, content} before trusting a record, and (iii) I will list control-plane (.hacp) authenticity as a non-goal, since signed freezes would be a HACP change. NITS: (1) the trust-boundary mermaid labels the UDS 'seal/open/sign', which contradicts F2 (no sign endpoint); should be seal/open/session. (2) Scope section 4 item 6 names docs/test-matrix.md; the frozen file is docs/hacp-secure-test-matrix.md, and the modules/threat-model/non-goals docs are docs/hacp-secure-*.md. (3) Architecture section 12.4 says a lost message 'stalls the stream until redelivered'; that is the F5 wedge, please update it once F5 settles. (4) The hello signature does not cover 'contract', yet hello carries it. Require contract == '' on hello/ack in the schema. (5) A replayed hello makes the responder allocate session state with no key confirmation until the first msg. Bound pending sessions per peer (I suggest 4, oldest evicted); I am adding this to the threat model. (6) Module split: I am proposing src/secure/client.rs (UDS client, no crypto deps) so the agent-facing hacp-secure binary structurally cannot link key-store code; please add it to section 10 if you agree.
